meta.source: UN Comtrade (partner-reported and Kiribati-reported HS6 monthly data)
notes: OFFLINE method (inferred_from_data). Publication status is inferred from the rows the pipeline holds: a partner counts as published for a month if it has at least one row with partner Kiribati in that month (any flow, or in the fish-only pull), or in any later month (Comtrade releases are cumulative).

A partner that published a dataset recording no trade with Kiribati in a month is indistinguishable from one that has not published; small partners therefore read as 'missing' more often than they really are, and the shares shown are a lower bound on true coverage.

Months Kiribati did not report (2019, 2021, 2022-01..2023-05, 2024-07, 2024-09, 2025-03, 2025-10) have no all-goods mirror pull; their status rests on the fish-only pull and the later-month rule and is labelled 'partial_fish_only'. Partners never observed (Other Asia, nes) count as not published.
Annual: a partner counts as published for a year if it appears in that year's annual fish or ships by-reporter table, or if at least 10 of its 12 months are counted as published.
The live refresh replaces this with Comtrade's data-availability service (coverage_method 'comtrade_getDa'), which answers the question directly.

definitions.share_count: number of panel partners whose dataset for the period is published, divided by the panel size
definitions.share_w_exports: same, weighting each partner by its share of partner-reported Kiribati exports in the reference window
definitions.share_w_imports: same, weighting by share of partner-reported Kiribati imports
definitions.quarterly: partner-months published / partner-months possible (3 per partner, also for an unfinished quarter)
definitions.annual: a partner counts as published for a year if its annual dataset exists, or at least 10 of its 12 monthly datasets do; for the current, unfinished year (basis 'year_in_progress') the shares are partner-months published / (12 x panel), so the year fills up like an unfinished quarter
